sections.title: Qualifications for Overseers
observations: This section outlines the essential qualities required for someone to serve as an overseer or elder in the church. The emphasis is on moral character, ability to teach, and a good reputation both inside and outside the church.
The call for overseers to be 'above reproach' indicates the high standard of integrity expected from church leaders. This sets a tone for the church's witness in the community.

sections.title: Qualifications for Deacons
observations: Similar to overseers, deacons are also held to a high standard of character. The qualifications include being dignified, not double-tongued, and not addicted to much wine.
The role of deacons is crucial in serving the church and supporting the ministry of the Word. Their character reflects the church's commitment to godliness.

sections.title: The Mystery of Godliness
observations: This section highlights the centrality of the gospel and the mystery of godliness. It emphasizes the importance of the church's foundation in the truth of Christ.
The mention of Christ's incarnation, resurrection, and ascension serves as a reminder of the core beliefs that should unite the church.

importantVerses.commentary: The saying is trustworthy: If anyone aspires to the office of overseer, he desires a noble task.
...the church of the living God, a pillar and buttress of the truth.

questions: What does it mean to be 'above reproach' in the context of church leadership?
How do the qualifications for overseers and deacons reflect the character of Christ?
In what ways can the church act as a 'pillar and buttress of the truth' in today's society?
